paper_metadata.title: Developing a machine learning Ni-Co-Al ternary interatomic potential for temperature and strain-rate dependent mechanical behaviors of Ni-based single crystal superalloys

evidence.quote: Ni-based single crystal (SX) superalloys, with excellent mechanical properties in high temperature, are widely used as the preferred materials in the aerospace field.

Structure optimization of the cubic model (Fig. 1a) was carried out under the periodic boundary conditions. Specifically, it was equilibrated for 200 ps with a time step of 1 fs under the NPT ensembles at various temperatures and 0 bar after energy minimization to minimize the artificial elastic stress field.

After the NPT equilibration, tensile loading was applied along x-direction at a constant strain rate 𝜀̇=2.5×10 8 s−1. Besides, two other strain rates 5×108 s−1 and 1×109 s−1 were also applied to examine the strain rate effect.
Firstly, the region from 𝑧= 0 to 1 nm was set as a rigid body and used as a shock head. The shock head impacted the model at a certain velocity under the NVE ensemble for 2 ps.
Then, the shock loading was removed and the free evolution continued for 20 ps under the NVE ensemble.
This model underwent uniaxial tensile simulations at 300 K, 600 K, 900 K, and 1200 K, at a strain rate of 2.5 × 108 s−1.

Nickel-based superalloys derive their exceptional high-temperature mechanical properties primarily from precipitation strengthening, where the lattice misfit-induced elastic stress fields and interfacial dislocation networks at 𝛾/𝛾′ phase boundaries (PBs) play a pivotal role.
